/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* (Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, §55) if every finite
set of its elements is contained in a finite normal subgroup. A family of subgroups
$(H_i)_{i \in I}$ *commutes elementwise* if $xy = yx$ whenever $x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$
and $i \neq j$. Since such subgroups normalise each other, their product is the subgroup
they generate, that is, their join $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} H_i$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

justification.closest_existing_considered: Monoid.IsTorsion (too weak: only says each element has finite order), Subgroup.Normal / Subgroup.normalClosure (building blocks only); no 'locally finite'/'locally normal' group predicate exists in Mathlib.GroupTheory.

justification.why_needed: Mathlib and FormalConjecturesForMathlib have no notion of a locally normal group (every finite set of elements is contained in a finite normal subgroup), which is the hypothesis of the problem. Defined as ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ S ⊆ N, with two proven `category test` lemmas (finite groups are locally normal; locally normal groups are torsion).

in a finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/

@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyNormal G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨N, -, hN, hx⟩ := hG {x} (Set.finite_singleton x)
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, hx rfl⟩ : N) := isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  exact Submonoid.isOfFinOrder_coe.2 h

@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry
blocks.docstring:
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, for every locally normal group $G$, is there a family $(H_i)_{i \in I}$ of
subgroups of $G$, each at most countable, such that $H_i$ and $H_j$ commute elementwise
for all $i \neq j$ and the derived subgroup $G' = [G, G]$ is the product of the $H_i$?
Since the $H_i$ commute elementwise, their product is the subgroup they generate, so
"$G'$ is the product of the $H_i$" is stated as $\bigsqcup_i H_i = G'$.

claims.decomposer_note: Single yes/no question (answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G locally normal, ∃ family of subgroups H_i of G, each at most countable, pairwise commuting elementwise (∀ i ≠ j, ∀ x ∈ H_i, y ∈ H_j, x*y = y*x), with ⨆ i, H_i = commutator G); 'locally normal' in Kourovka usage means every finite subset (equivalently every finitely generated subgroup) lies in a finite normal subgroup, the family of subgroups may be infinite (arbitrary index type) so 'product' means the subgroup generated (join) of the pairwise elementwise-commuting subgroups, and 'at most countable' means Countable as a set (finite allowed).
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates state the same (equivalent) proposition: answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ G : Type, [Group G], locally normal (every finite set of elements lies in a finite normal subgroup, Kurosh's definition) → ∃ ι : Type, H : ι → Subgroup G, each H i at most countable, elementwise commuting for i ≠ j, and ⨆ i, H i = commutator G. Checked: derived subgroup = commutator G; 'at most countable' applies to each factor (the 'countably many factors' reading would be trivially true via H = G'); join equals the group-theoretic product for pairwise elementwise-commuting subgroups; commutation required only for i ≠ j so factors need not be abelian (repeated entries can be reindexed, so no loss); answer(True) is the positive answer; abelian G handled by empty ι (⨆ = ⊥ = commutator G); not trivially true. c02 chosen on style: documented bespoke IsLocallyNormal, two test lemmas (finite groups are locally normal; locally normal ⇒ torsion, which validates the definition), explicit i ≠ j quantifier, Countable on the subgroup. Minor edit: module docstring expanded with the Kurosh reference and the definition of elementwise commutation.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Conjecture 6.9

by Yu. M. Gorchakov

Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

Here a group is *locally normal* (Kurosh, *The Theory of Groups*, §55) if every finite
set of its elements is contained in a finite normal subgroup. A family of subgroups
$(H_i)_{i \in I}$ *commutes elementwise* if $xy = yx$ whenever $x \in H_i$, $y \in H_j$
and $i \neq j$. Since such subgroups normalise each other, their product is the subgroup
they generate, that is, their join $\bigsqcup_{i \in I} H_i$.

*Reference:* [The Kourovka Notebook](https://arxiv.org/abs/1401.0300v46)
-/

namespace Kourovka.«6.9»

/-- A group $G$ is *locally normal* if every finite set of elements of $G$ is contained
in a finite normal subgroup of $G$. -/
def IsLocallyNormal (G : Type*) [Group G] : Prop :=
  ∀ S : Set G, S.Finite → ∃ N : Subgroup G, N.Normal ∧ Finite N ∧ S ⊆ N

/-- Every finite group is locally normal. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.of_finite (G : Type*) [Group G] [Finite G] : IsLocallyNormal G :=
  fun _ _ => ⟨⊤, inferInstance, inferInstance, fun _ _ => Subgroup.mem_top _⟩

/-- Every locally normal group is a torsion group. -/
@[category test, AMS 20]
theorem IsLocallyNormal.isTorsion {G : Type*} [Group G] (hG : IsLocallyNormal G) :
    Monoid.IsTorsion G := by
  intro x
  obtain ⟨N, -, hN, hx⟩ := hG {x} (Set.finite_singleton x)
  have h : IsOfFinOrder (⟨x, hx rfl⟩ : N) := isOfFinOrder_of_finite _
  exact Submonoid.isOfFinOrder_coe.2 h

/--
Is the derived subgroup of any locally normal group decomposable into a product of
at most countable subgroups which commute elementwise?

That is, for every locally normal group $G$, is there a family $(H_i)_{i \in I}$ of
subgroups of $G$, each at most countable, such that $H_i$ and $H_j$ commute elementwise
for all $i \neq j$ and the derived subgroup $G' = [G, G]$ is the product of the $H_i$?
Since the $H_i$ commute elementwise, their product is the subgroup they generate, so
"$G'$ is the product of the $H_i$" is stated as $\bigsqcup_i H_i = G'$.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 20]
theorem kourovka.«6.9» : answer(sorry) ↔
    ∀ (G : Type) [Group G], IsLocallyNormal G →
      ∃ (ι : Type) (H : ι → Subgroup G),
        (∀ i, Countable (H i)) ∧
        (∀ i j, i ≠ j → ∀ x ∈ H i, ∀ y ∈ H j, Commute x y) ∧
        ⨆ i, H i = commutator G := by
  sorry

end Kourovka.«6.9»

items: 'Locally normal' is formalized via finite subsets of G (∀ S finite, ∃ finite normal N ⊇ S), following the table's note; this is equivalent to the single-element version (every element lies in a finite normal subgroup) since a product of finitely many finite normal subgroups is a finite normal subgroup.

'Product of subgroups which commute elementwise' is rendered as the join ⨆ i, H i of a family indexed by an arbitrary type ι : Type (sufficient since G : Type, so any family of subgroups can be reindexed in Type). No directness (trivial intersections) is imposed, as the source says only 'product'.

Pairwise commutation is stated for indices i ≠ j (so repeated subgroups in the family would be forced to be abelian); this is equivalent to the set-based 'pairwise distinct subgroups commute' formulation after deduplication.
'At most countable' is `Countable (H i)` on the coerced subtype, which allows finite subgroups.
The subgroups H i are subgroups of G rather than of the derived subgroup; since their join equals commutator G, each H i ≤ commutator G automatically.

reviewer_notes: No candidate omitted the slot and none raised decomposition objections; all compiled. The statement is unambiguous modulo two conventions, both resolved as in the table notes: 'locally normal' = Kurosh's sense (every finite subset in a finite normal subgroup; equivalently locally finite FC-group), and 'product' of a possibly infinite elementwise-commuting family = the subgroup generated (join), which coincides with the set of finite products. 'Direct' is not required by the source (it says 'product', with commutation stated separately), so no trivial-intersection condition was added. G and ι live in Type, following the existing Kourovka files (1_40, 19_25, 20_76). Bespoke IsLocallyNormal kept in the problem file as 1_40.lean does with IsEngelGroup; a maintainer may prefer to move it to FormalConjecturesForMathlib.
